agree.reason: A dentist with an empty manager's chair would find this credible, but it leaves out the two points most likely to win him over: she can start within two weeks and work the Tuesday and Thursday evenings.

honest.reason: Most claims follow the brief, but 'led' the move to software (the brief says 'handled'), 'kept the office running smoothly throughout the change' and 'busy practice' are embellishments the facts don't support.

works_the_facts.reason: It repeats the $38,000-to-$9,000 drop without working out the stronger form, a cut of more than three-quarters or about $29,000 recovered, and it never sets 14 staff against the 9 she would supervise.

right_comparison.reason: It mentions four vets and fourteen staff but never sets them against Brookside's three dentists and nine staff, which would show the new job as a step within her proven range.

qualification.reason: The Dentrix commitment names the course and its roughly 20 hours and promises it will be done before day one, which he can check, but it gives no date and says nothing about what follows if it is late.

objections.reason: It deals with the gap and with Dentrix, but on the doubt about whether her skills are current it leaves out her four years as church treasurer keeping the books in QuickBooks, and it gives no reference, such as Dr. Kim, to back her record.

fit.reason: It is a proper cover letter well under 300 words, but it leaves '[Your Name]' as a placeholder even though her name was known.
